Last updated November 14, 2026.

Scottsdale at a glance

  • Estimated population, July 1, 2025: 243,006 (Census Bureau).
Selling in Scottsdale?

What are your options for selling a house fast in Scottsdale, AZ?

You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house as-is. In Scottsdale the right choice depends on how much the house needs, because the median owner-occupied home value is $789,800 and a repair bill on a home that size can be large.

A listing usually brings the widest pool of buyers and the highest price for a house in good shape. A cash sale trades some of that price for speed and certainty, and it suits owners facing a relocation, an inherited property, a tenant problem or a stalled renovation. Ask each buyer for the net figure after repairs, fees and carrying costs, then compare the totals.

How is Scottsdale laid out, and why does it matter for a sale?

Scottsdale is long and narrow: about 31 miles from north to south across 184.5 square miles, with Phoenix on the west, Tonto National Forest to the north, the McDowell Mountains on the east and the Salt River to the south. It was named in 1894 for Winfield Scott, an Army chaplain, and incorporated in 1951 with about 2,000 residents. The Census Bureau now estimates 243,006 residents as of July 1, 2025.

The city is commonly split into four areas, and buyers shop them differently:

  • South Scottsdale, from McKellips Road north to Thomas Road, includes the SkySong research center tied to Arizona State University
  • Old Town, the downtown core of galleries, restaurants and older streets
  • Central Scottsdale, also called the Shea Corridor, from Camelback Road north to Shea Boulevard
  • North Scottsdale, the northern end of the city

Say which area your house is in when you ask for offers. Comparable sales a mile apart can be far apart in price.

What does Census data say about Scottsdale housing?

Scottsdale is an older, higher-income city with small households and a large share of retirees. The figures below are Census Bureau numbers for 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

MeasureScottsdale
Population, July 1, 2025 estimate243,006
Households118,637
Persons per household2.03
Owner-occupied housing rate67.0%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$789,800
Median gross rent$2,013
Median household income$110,886
Residents age 65 and over26.4%

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Scottsdale city, Arizona.

With 67 percent of homes owner-occupied, about one in three households rents, so rentals are a real part of the market and some buyers will want to know what a house can earn.

Which employers, schools and roads shape Scottsdale buyer demand?

Health care, finance, defense and tourism anchor the local economy. The city's 2022 financial report listed HonorHealth (7,131 employees), Vanguard (2,770), General Dynamics Mission Systems (2,700), the City of Scottsdale (2,612), the Scottsdale Unified School District (2,093) and the Mayo Clinic (1,917) as its top employers. The Scottsdale Airpark around the municipal airport is a major employment center, and winter visitors from colder states often end up buying second homes here. The Census Bureau counted $3,062,966,000 in accommodation and food services sales in 2022, which shows how much the visitor economy matters, and the mean commute for workers is 21.6 minutes.

Public schools are split among several districts, which is worth stating in any listing:

  • Scottsdale Unified serves most of the city and runs five high schools: Arcadia, Coronado, Chaparral, Desert Mountain and Saguaro
  • Paradise Valley Unified serves North Scottsdale, including Horizon and Pinnacle high schools
  • Cave Creek Unified, Fountain Hills Unified, Balsz Elementary and Phoenix Union High School districts cover other pieces

Loop 101 is the main freeway, Valley Metro runs the regional buses, and the city operates a free Downtown Trolley and Neighborhood Trolley. Climate is dry desert, with a mean July high near 104 degrees and about 8.7 inches of rain a year.

Can a buyer rent your Scottsdale house short term?

Yes, but Scottsdale requires a city license for any rental under 30 days. A buyer who plans nightly or weekly stays should know the steps before bidding, and a seller can use them as a selling point. The annual license costs $250 per property, and rentals of 30 days or longer do not need it.

The city lists these steps for an operator:

  • Get a Transaction Privilege Tax license from the Arizona Department of Revenue for each rental, listing Scottsdale (SC) as a region code
  • Apply for the Scottsdale license under Ordinance 4566
  • Within 30 days of receiving it, notify the neighbors beside and across the street, and carry at least $500,000 in liability coverage
  • Register the property with the Maricopa County Assessor before anyone occupies it
  • Post the required notice inside the front door and the backyard door

Properties with a pool, hot tub or spa also face pool barrier rules. State law (A.R.S. 9-500.39) limits what a city can require, and it caps a permit fee at the actual cost or $250, whichever is less. Ask the City of Scottsdale licensing office whether a license already exists for your address.

How do you record a Scottsdale sale in Maricopa County?

The deed is recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder, and it needs a completed affidavit of property value unless an exemption is noted on it (A.R.S. 11-1133). The affidavit gives the price, financing, parcel number, sale date and whether the home will be owner-occupied or rented. A.R.S. 11-1134 exempts, among other transfers, a deed of gift and a transfer with only nominal consideration between parent and child, spouses or siblings.

The Recorder lists a $30 fee for most documents, $1 per page for copies and $3 for a certification. Your title or escrow company normally handles the filing and tells you the exact amount on the closing statement.

When is Maricopa County property tax due for a Scottsdale owner?

Tax bills are due in two halves, October 1 and March 1, and become delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and May 1 (A.R.S. 42-18052). The Maricopa County Treasurer's 2026 calendar shows first-half taxes delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 2, 2026, so that date has passed. Final delinquent notices for unpaid 2025 taxes go out December 1, and December 31 is the last day to pay 2026 full-year taxes of more than $100 without interest.

Ask the Maricopa County Treasurer for a current balance on your parcel before you list, and have your title company explain how the current year is divided at closing.

More questions about Scottsdale, AZ

How fast can a Scottsdale house sell for cash?

A cash sale can close faster than a financed one, because there is no lender appraisal or loan approval. The actual date depends on the title search, any liens or probate steps, and when both sides sign. Ask the buyer to give you a written closing date.

Do I need a Scottsdale license to sell a house that was a short-term rental?

The license covers operating a rental of under 30 days, so ask the City of Scottsdale licensing office what happens to yours when the property sells. A new owner who continues short-term renting should expect to apply for their own.

What does it cost to record a deed in Maricopa County?

The Maricopa County Recorder lists $30 for most documents. Copies are $1 per page and a certification is $3. Arizona sets the same $30 fee by statute in A.R.S. 11-475.

Which school district is my Scottsdale home in?

It depends on the street. Scottsdale Unified serves most of the city, Paradise Valley Unified serves North Scottsdale, and parts belong to Cave Creek, Fountain Hills, Balsz and Phoenix Union districts. Check your address with the district before you advertise a school.

Are Scottsdale property taxes still open for 2026?

The first half of 2026 became delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 2, 2026. Maricopa County lists December 31 as the last day to pay full-year 2026 taxes without interest, and the second half is due March 1, 2027. Contact the County Treasurer for your balance.

How can you sell a house fast in Surprise, AZ?

You can list it with an agent, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as-is. In Surprise, a house in good shape tends to suit a listing, and a house that needs work or has a deadline attached tends to suit a direct sale.

Surprise is a city in Maricopa County. The Census Bureau estimates 175,304 residents as of July 1, 2025, and 79.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Median value for an owner-occupied home is $435,100. When you gather offers, ask each buyer to state the closing date, who pays recording and title charges, and whether repairs are priced in.

How did Surprise grow into a city of 175,000?

Surprise grew from a farm settlement into one of the larger cities in the state within about a generation. It was founded in 1938 by Flora Mae Statler, incorporated as a town on December 12, 1960, and first built as inexpensive housing for agricultural workers. The original townsite is bounded by Greenway Road on the south, El Mirage Road on the east, Bell Road on the north and Dysart Road on the west. City Hall now stands on the site of a former auxiliary airfield for Luke Air Force Base, and the old runway outlines still show in aerial photos.

YearPopulation
2000 census30,848
2010 census117,517
2020 census143,148
July 1, 2025 estimate175,304

Source: U.S. Census Bureau decennial counts and QuickFacts.

How the town got its name is still debated. Some records say Statler chose it because she would be surprised if the town ever amounted to much, while others point to Surprise, Nebraska, the hometown of her husband Homer Ludden. Local government is a mayor elected at large and a six-member council elected by district, in staggered four-year terms. The city library system, created in 2023 when Surprise took over three county libraries, includes the Surprise Regional Library on the Recreation Campus and branches in the original townsite and in north Surprise.

The city covers 110.5 square miles at 1,385 feet of elevation. Population is up 22.5 percent from the April 2020 estimates base, so much of the housing is recent construction, and a buyer will compare yours with newer homes.

What do the Census numbers show for Surprise housing?

Surprise skews toward owners, families and retirees at once. The Census Bureau reports these figures for 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

  • Households: 56,506, averaging 2.71 persons
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $435,100
  • Median gross rent: $2,033
  • Median household income: $96,711
  • Residents under 18: 23.1 percent; age 65 and over: 22.2 percent
  • Mean commute to work: 30.2 minutes

The long commute matters when you describe the house. Many residents work elsewhere in the Valley, so the distance to Loop 303, U.S. 60 and the Valley Metro express route to Glendale belongs in your listing.

A large age-restricted community also sits inside the city. Sun City Grand, for residents 45 and older, was founded in 1996, finished building homes in 2005 and has four golf courses. If your house is inside it, ask the community for its resale rules before you accept an offer.

Which schools, jobs and roads draw buyers to Surprise?

The Dysart Unified School District serves most of the city, and the Nadaburg Unified School District serves a small section in the north. Confirm which one applies to your address before you advertise a school. Ottawa University opened a campus in Surprise in 2017.

The largest employers in the 2023 Council of Governments database were:

  • Dysart Unified School District, 1,760 employees
  • City of Surprise, 1,170
  • Walmart, 890
  • Sun Health Foundation, 570
  • Fry's Food and Drug, 550

A foreign trade zone at the southeast corner of the city, the Southwest Railplex industrial district, has rail access through BNSF. Roads are Loop 303 and U.S. 60. Valley Metro runs express route 571 between Surprise and Glendale, and the WeRIDE on-demand service had been scheduled to end on July 1, 2025.

Which Surprise city offices matter when you sell or rent a house?

Planning, permits and building safety all sit in the city's Community Development Department. Its Permits and Applications page covers everything from a commercial project to a resident adding a patio, and Building Inspections and Plan Review covers construction inspections. If you have an open permit or finished work without one, ask Community Development to clarify before you list.

The city also runs a Rental Accountability Ordinance, which sits under Code Enforcement along with a page on sober living homes. If the house is currently rented, ask Surprise Code Enforcement what that ordinance requires of you and what a buyer inherits. Arizona law (A.R.S. 9-500.39) separately restricts what cities may require of short-term rentals, allowing a permit with a fee of no more than $250 or the cost of issuing it, an emergency contact and proof of $500,000 in liability insurance.

How is a Surprise sale recorded in Maricopa County?

A deed is recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder. A.R.S. 11-1133 requires a completed affidavit of property value with the deed, signed by buyer and seller or their agents, and the recorder must refuse the deed without it unless an exemption is noted. A.R.S. 11-1134 exempts transfers such as a deed of gift, a nominal-consideration transfer between family members, and a conveyance made under a court order.

Maricopa County charges $30 to record most documents, $1 per page for copies and $3 for a certification. Title or escrow companies normally file for you, and your closing statement will show the exact charges.

When are property taxes due for a Surprise homeowner?

Maricopa County collects in two halves due October 1 and March 1, with delinquency after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and May 1, moved to the next business day when those fall on a weekend (A.R.S. 42-18052). For 2026 the Treasurer's calendar shows the first half delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 2, a date already behind us. It also shows December 1 for final delinquent notices on unpaid 2025 taxes and December 31 as the last day to pay 2026 full-year taxes over $100 without interest. A full-year bill of $100 or less is delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on December 31.

Ask the Maricopa County Treasurer for the balance on your parcel before signing, and have the title company explain how the current year is divided between you and the buyer.

More questions about Surprise, AZ

Is Surprise a good place to sell a house quickly?

Speed depends on condition, price and how you sell. The city has grown 22.5 percent since the April 2020 estimates base, so there are many nearby comparable sales to price against. Compare the net amount from a listing, a private sale and a cash offer.

Which county records a Surprise home sale?

Maricopa County. The Maricopa County Recorder records the deed, and the fee for most documents is $30. The deed needs an affidavit of property value or a written exemption under Arizona law.

Do I need a permit to sell a house with unpermitted work in Surprise?

Ask the Surprise Community Development Department how the city handles work done without a permit. Unpermitted work can come up in a buyer's inspection or a lender's review, so tell the buyer what you know.

Which school district serves my Surprise address?

Most of the city is in the Dysart Unified School District, and a small northern section is in the Nadaburg Unified School District. Confirm your address with the district before you list.

Can I sell a rented house in Surprise with tenants in it?

Check your lease and your notice duties first, and ask Surprise Code Enforcement about the Rental Accountability Ordinance. A buyer who wants the tenants kept should say so in writing before you accept an offer.

How do you sell a house fast in Maricopa, AZ?

Maricopa sellers can move quickly by deciding between a listing and a direct cash sale, then handling HOA paperwork and permit questions before an offer arrives. The city is in Pinal County, so county offices, tax dates and recording all follow Pinal County rather than Maricopa County.

The Census Bureau estimated 78,362 residents on July 1, 2025, up 34.8 percent from the April 2020 base, and counted 83.6 percent of homes as owner-occupied. The median value of an owner-occupied home for 2020 to 2024 was $377,200, per QuickFacts.

Prepare these before you list or take a cash offer:

  • HOA contact, assessment amount and any special assessment notice
  • Loan payoff statements and any lien releases
  • Permits and final inspection records for pools, patios and garage conversions
  • Solar lease or battery lease paperwork, if any
  • The latest Pinal County property tax statement

How did Maricopa grow into a Pinal County city?

Maricopa sits in the Gila River Valley on flat ground at about 1,190 feet, with mountain ranges 10 to 20 miles away, per Wikipedia. It was a stage and rail stop long before it was a suburb. Maricopa Wells served travelers on the Butterfield Overland Mail route, and the first train left Maricopa for Phoenix on July 4, 1887. The city's own general plan adds that Father Kino described the area in 1694 and that cotton was king in the 1950s and 1960s.

In the 1970s and 1980s farmland was sold to developers who divided it into 3 1/3 acre mini-farms. The city incorporated on October 15, 2003, the 88th municipality in Arizona, with a population that had been 1,040 in 2000. It reached 43,482 in 2010 and 58,125 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 78,362.

The same plan says most residents work outside farming and commute to Casa Grande or the Phoenix area. It also reports that home occupations made up 60 percent of Maricopa's businesses in 2015, and it names the USDA Arid-Land Agricultural Research Center and the University of Arizona Maricopa Agricultural Center as local research employers.

What roads and transit do Maricopa buyers care about?

State Route 347, called John Wayne Parkway inside the city, is the main road. It connects to Interstate 10 about 14 miles north. State Route 84 lies 11 miles south and leads to Interstate 8, while State Route 238 runs west toward Mobile and Gila Bend. The Maricopa-Casa Grande Highway links the city to Casa Grande.

The Union Pacific line runs through the city, and Maricopa has an Amtrak station served by the Sunset Limited and Texas Eagle, the closest of those stops to Phoenix, with Amtrak Thruway connections to Phoenix. The city runs Maricopa Express Transit, a local bus service. The mean travel time to work is 36.6 minutes, so commute details belong in listing copy.

What permits and building codes affect a Maricopa sale?

The city's Permit Center at 39700 W Civic Center Plaza handles construction applications, and all plan submittals are digital through its online portal. It is open Monday through Thursday from 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. and closed Fridays. Call (520) 316-6920 or email dsd@maricopa-az.gov to ask about permit history for your address, per the city's Permit Center page.

Building rules changed this year. The council adopted the 2024 International Codes, the 2023 National Electrical Code and the A117.1-2017 accessibility standard on January 20, 2026, effective February 20, 2026. Residential standard plans approved under the 2018 codes stayed valid only until September 1, 2026, which has now passed. Permits issued under the 2018 codes that sat idle for 180 days could receive a one-time 180-day extension if the owner applied within 60 days of expiration, according to the city's public notice. The notice names Dale Garcia, the Building Official, at 520-316-6932.

If you are selling a house with an expired or unfinished permit, ask the Permit Center what it takes to close it under the codes now in force. Ask Development Services whether a short-term rental at your address needs a zoning permit or a license. State law at A.R.S. 9-500.39 bars a city from prohibiting short-term rentals but lets it require an emergency contact, neighbor notice and a permit fee capped at actual cost or $250.

How does an HOA sale work in Maricopa?

Many Maricopa houses sit in planned communities. For an association with 50 or more properties, A.R.S. 33-1806 has you give the association written notice that you accepted an offer, with the buyer's contact details. The association then has ten days to send the buyer its governing documents, budget, recent board minutes, financial statements, assessment amounts, any lien and any unresolved violation on your lot.

At closing the buyer signs an acknowledgment that the buyer is bound by the community's covenants and may face collection and foreclosure if assessments go unpaid. The association may charge the seller no more than $400 for the package, with a rush fee of up to $100 and an update fee of up to $50. A deed that carries certain exemptions under A.R.S. 11-1134 is excused from this process.

Call the HOA manager before you list and ask for a statement of your balance. A violation notice for paint, landscaping or a parked vehicle is easier to cure before a buyer sees it in the package.

How are deeds, taxes and schools handled for Maricopa homes?

Deeds for Maricopa go to the Pinal County Recorder. The county's fee schedule lists $30 for any document, and that amount covers the affidavit of property value. The affidavit is required by A.R.S. 11-1133 unless the deed bears an exemption notation. Title or escrow staff normally handle recording on the closing date.

The Pinal County Treasurer's dates page sets the schedule:

  • Taxes over $100 can be paid in two halves. The first is due October 1 and delinquent after 5 p.m. on November 1. Because November 1, 2026 was a Sunday, that deadline moved to Monday, November 2 and has passed.
  • The second half is due March 1 and delinquent after May 1.
  • Full-year payments are due by December 31.
  • The late penalty is 16 percent a year, prorated monthly, and property with delinquent taxes can be offered at the county's online tax lien sale in February.

The Treasurer notes that Arizona law does not require a mailed bill, so make sure the Assessor has your correct address, at 520-866-6361. Ask your escrow officer how the year's tax will be split between you and the buyer.

The Maricopa Unified School District serves more than 9,950 students from preschool through grade 12 and calls itself the largest employer in the city. It lists Santa Rosa Elementary's dual language program, Desert Wind and Maricopa Wells middle schools and the new Alma Farrell Innovation Academy, the district's first K-8.

More questions about Maricopa, AZ

Is Maricopa, AZ in Maricopa County?

No. The city of Maricopa is in Pinal County. Recording goes through the Pinal County Recorder, property tax goes through the Pinal County Treasurer, and the Pinal County Assessor handles ownership and address changes.

When are Pinal County property taxes due?

The first half is due October 1 and delinquent after 5 p.m. on November 1, and the second half is due March 1 and delinquent after May 1. When a date lands on a weekend, it moves to the next business day. Full-year taxes are due by December 31.

Can I sell a Maricopa house that has an open permit?

Yes, but the buyer may ask you to close it first. Contact the Permit Center at (520) 316-6920 for the permit history at your address. The city adopted new building codes effective February 20, 2026, and permits issued under the older codes have their own extension rules.

How much will my HOA charge when I sell?

State law lets the association charge the seller up to $400 for the resale package and lien statement, up to $100 more for a rush within 72 hours and up to $50 for an update. The fees are collected at or after the close of escrow and charged once per transaction.

What is the recording fee for a deed in Pinal County?

The Pinal County Recorder lists $30 for any document required or authorized to be recorded. The fee includes the affidavit of property value and $1 of postage for mailing the document back. Your escrow company normally pays this at closing.

How do you sell a house fast in Marana, AZ?

A Marana seller moves fastest by picking a sale route first, either an agent listing or a direct cash sale, and then clearing the HOA, tax and title items that tend to hold up closings. Marana is a growing town northwest of Tucson with a lot of newer subdivisions, so check early whether your house is in an HOA.

The Census Bureau estimated 65,523 residents on July 1, 2025, up 26.2 percent from the April 2020 base. Owners occupy 83.7 percent of homes, and the median value of an owner-occupied home for 2020 to 2024 was $413,800, per QuickFacts. A listing exposes the house to the widest group of buyers. What should sellers know about Marana's size and history?

Marana lies mostly in Pima County, with a small piece in Pinal County, and stretches along Interstate 10 from the county line to the Tucson city limits. It covers about 121 square miles of land among the Tortolita, Santa Catalina and Tucson mountains and includes the Dove Mountain area. Phoenix is roughly 90 minutes northwest by Interstate 10, per Wikipedia.

Farming shaped the place. The area was first called Postvale, and cotton, wheat, barley, alfalfa and pecans grew here. The town incorporated about 10 square miles in March 1977, and 1,500 residents elected the first council that August. A targeted annexation policy began in 1979. In 1992 the council annexed a corridor along Interstate 10, Ina Road and Thornydale Road, and the Pima County Superior Court upheld that annexation in 1994.

The town's own profile page describes Marana as a logistics location on Interstate 10 and the Union Pacific Railroad, with a regional general aviation airport and a planned downtown. It names the Ritz-Carlton at Dove Mountain, Heritage Park and the Santa Cruz River Path as local landmarks. Those features are what buyers cite when they compare Marana with other parts of the Tucson area.

Does flood history matter when selling a Marana house?

It can. Marana suffered severe flash flooding during Tropical Storm Claudia in 1962, and in 1983 Tropical Storm Octave flooded Marana and four other Arizona towns almost entirely. The Octave system is considered the cause of the worst flood in Pima County history.

Flood risk today varies lot by lot. A buyer, lender or insurer will want to know whether the property sits in a mapped FEMA floodplain, so look up your parcel before you list and keep any flood insurance paperwork handy. If the house is in an unincorporated area rather than inside town limits, Arizona's A.R.S. 33-422 applies to sellers of five or fewer parcels other than subdivided land. It requires a written affidavit of disclosure at least seven days before transfer, covering legal and physical access, road maintenance, floodplain status, utilities, wells and septic systems, and it gives the buyer a five-day right to rescind.

If the house is in a planned community, the HOA sets part of your timeline. Smaller communities have the seller deliver the information within the same ten days.

The association may charge the seller up to $400 for the resale package and lien statement, plus up to $100 for a rush within 72 hours and $50 for an update after 30 days. Fees are collected at the close of escrow and cannot be charged twice for one transaction. The buyer signs a statement at closing acknowledging the community's covenants and assessments. Ask the HOA manager for the package early, because an unpaid assessment shows up as a lien that comes out of your proceeds.

Ask the Town's Development Services Center for the permit history on your address, especially for pools, casitas, solar and garage work, and close any open permits before a buyer's inspector finds them.   • A neighbor notification attestation emailed to licensing@maranaaz.gov before the rental start date
  • Annual renewal, with an invoice mailed 30 days before expiration, and updates to the Town within 10 days of any change

If you have operated a short-term rental, give the buyer the license and registration details. A buyer who plans to rent should ask the Town's licensing staff what a new application needs.

How are deeds recorded and property taxes billed for Marana homes?

Most Marana deeds are recorded with the Pima County Recorder. The fee page lists a flat $30 recording fee under A.R.S. 11-475 and a $5 fee to return documents submitted improperly. It says the Affidavit of Property Value form comes from the Arizona Department of Revenue. State law requires the affidavit with a transfer deed unless the deed shows an exemption, under A.R.S. 11-1133. For the small part of Marana in Pinal County, the Pinal County Recorder charges $30 for any document, and that fee already covers the affidavit of property value.

Pima County sent its 2026 bills by the end of September. Its property tax page lists these dates:

  • First half due October 1, 2026, delinquent November 2, 2026. That date has passed.
  • Full-year payment due December 31, 2026.
  • Second half due March 1, 2027, delinquent May 3, 2027.

The Pima Treasurer's office takes online payments at to.pima.gov or by phone at 520-724-8341, and charges a 1.95 percent convenience fee on card payments with a $1.95 minimum, or $0.50 for an eCheck. Address changes for tax bills go through the Pima County Assessor. Pinal County parcels follow Pinal's own schedule, with the first half delinquent after 5 p.m. on November 1 and the second half after May 1.

Which schools serve Marana homes?

Most of the town is in the Marana Unified School District, which serves grades preK to 12 from an office at 11279 W. Grier Road. Flowing Wells Unified covers the far southeastern edge of the town, and the portion in Pinal County is served by Red Rock Elementary and Santa Cruz Valley Union High School districts. Confirm the district with a street address search before you list.

Yes. The HOA's resale statement lists any unpaid assessment lien, and your escrow officer can pay it from your proceeds if you agree. Ask the association for its statement early, since the association has ten days after notice of a pending sale to deliver the resale package to the buyer.

How much does it cost to record a deed for a Marana property?

The Pima County Recorder lists $30 per document, and the Pinal County Recorder lists the same $30. The Affidavit of Property Value is required unless the deed shows an exemption. Your escrow or title company normally pays and files these at closing.

Is Marana in Pima County or Pinal County?

Mostly Pima County, with a small portion in Pinal County. Pima County bills most Marana homes, while the Pinal County Treasurer bills parcels in the Pinal portion. Look at your tax statement to see which county issues your bill and which due dates apply.

Did I miss the first-half property tax deadline for Marana in 2026?

If your home is in Pima County, the first half was due October 1 and became delinquent after November 2, 2026, which has passed. Interest accrues after that date. Check the Pima Treasurer's site for the exact amount. If you have not paid, paying both halves by December 31 waives interest accrued after November 1.

The city is built around a lake, a bridge and a retiree population, so buyer expectations differ from a typical Arizona suburb.

The Census Bureau counted 57,144 residents in 2020 and estimated 59,358 on July 1, 2025. Residents 65 and over make up 35.2 percent of the population, households average 2.04 people, and 73.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The median value of an owner-occupied home for 2020 to 2024 was $455,400, according to QuickFacts.

Before you choose a route, collect the documents a buyer or escrow officer will ask for:

What should sellers know about the city's layout and history?

Lake Havasu City sits on the east side of Lake Havasu, a reservoir on the Colorado River, about 60 miles south of Kingman and 193 miles northwest of Phoenix. The city covers 46.34 square miles of land. The only surface access is Arizona State Route 95, which meets Interstate 40 19 miles to the north and Interstate 10 74 miles to the south, per Wikipedia.

The town started in 1963 by resolution of the Mohave County Board of Supervisors and incorporated in 1978. Robert P. McCulloch bought 3,353 acres on Pittsburgh Point in 1958, later acquired about 13,000 more acres of federal land, and flew prospective buyers in for free. His company bought London Bridge from the City of London for $2.5 million and had it reassembled here, and the bridge opened on October 5, 1971. C. V. Wood, the designer of Disneyland, laid out the road system.

Lots have been sold here since the 1960s, so some houses are decades old. Your own record of past upgrades answers a buyer's questions about wiring, plumbing and roofs.

How does the desert heat affect a house in Lake Havasu City?

Lake Havasu City has one of the hottest climates in Arizona, and a buyer will check the cooling system first. The state's record high of 128 degrees Fahrenheit was recorded here on June 29, 1994. Summer days routinely reach 110 degrees, temperatures can pass 100 as early as April and as late as October, and overnight lows in July and August often stay between 80 and 90 degrees.

Mean annual rainfall is only about 4.16 inches, and winter highs usually run in the 60s and 70s. Dry air and strong sun are hard on roofing, exterior paint, window seals and pool equipment.

  • Keep service receipts for the air conditioner and any recent replacement.
  • Note the age and type of the roof covering, and any repairs.
  • Photograph the condition of pool plaster, pumps and fencing.
  • Save your electric and water bills for the hottest months, since buyers ask about summer costs.

These records help a buyer judge risk, and they also support your asking price when an offer comes in lower than expected.

Which permits and city rules matter before selling in Lake Havasu City?

The Building Permits page lists the jobs that need a permit. They include room additions, patio covers, detached structures over 200 square feet, swimming pools and spas, gas lines, electrical panel change-outs, rewires, photovoltaic systems, fireplace installations, wall removal and added or relocated plumbing fixtures. Retaining walls over 2 feet 6 inches on a slope, or 3 feet on level ground, also need one.

Smaller jobs do not. The city lists painting, floor covering, minor drywall repair, replacing roof covering, replacing an existing water heater and replacing an existing air conditioner without increasing its weight, capacity, location or ampacity as work that needs no permit. If you find an unpermitted pool or addition in your own history, email the Development Services office to request permit records for the address, or call 928-453-4148 and ask for the building group.

Current review times posted by the city are 30 business days for a single-family home or duplex, 20 for a residential addition, garage or patio cover, and 10 for pools, retaining walls and mechanical, electrical and plumbing permits, with repeat reviews of residential plans at 5 business days. That matters if a buyer asks you to close an open permit before closing.

The Code Enforcement page names issues that trip up sellers: unscreened unlicensed vehicles, trash or debris visible from the street, structures in setback areas, and living in an RV or travel trailer for more than 7 days per calendar quarter on an improved residential lot. Fix any open complaint before listing. Trash cans may go to the curb no more than 12 hours before pickup.

State law caps what the city may do. A first verified violation can bring a penalty of up to $500 or one night's advertised rent, whichever is greater.

If you have rented the house by the night, tell buyers and hand over the license number, tax registration and insurance details. If you have not, say so plainly. For a current permit fee or ordinance requirement, ask the city's licensing office, since the code and fee schedule can change.

At the Mohave County Recorder office at 2001 College Drive, Suite 93, or at the main office in Kingman. The county lists a $30 fee, and the deed needs an Affidavit of Property Value or an exemption number. Your title company usually handles this for you at closing.

How do you sell a house fast in Sierra Vista, AZ?

Sierra Vista has one feature that sets its market apart from other Arizona cities: Fort Huachuca, the Army post at the northwest edge of town, which drives a steady cycle of arrivals and departures.

The Census Bureau counts 7,133 veterans in the city and estimates 44,907 residents as of July 1, 2025. That is 0.9 percent below the April 2020 estimates base of 45,310, so the population is flat rather than growing, which is worth keeping in mind when you set a price. If a permanent change of station, a deployment or a family move sets your deadline, ask each buyer for a written closing date as well as a price.

Where is Sierra Vista and what is it like?

Sierra Vista is the commercial center of Cochise County, in the southwest corner of the county about 75 miles southeast of Tucson. Tombstone is 15 miles northeast and Bisbee 20 miles southeast, and the Mexican border is about 15 miles south. The city covers 152.5 square miles at 4,623 feet of elevation, with the Huachuca Mountains on the southwest side and the San Pedro River just east of the city limits. State Routes 90 and 92 are the main roads.

The area grew around Camp Huachuca, founded in 1877, and the post was annexed into the city in 1971. Nearly half of local jobs are government jobs, the professional and technical services sector is large because of Army contracts, and Wick Communications, a newspaper publisher, is headquartered here. The Mall at Sierra Vista and several big-box retailers make the city the shopping hub for the county.

At that elevation the weather is milder than the Phoenix area. Winter lows average 20 to 30 degrees, frost can last into mid or late April, and the July and August monsoon delivers almost half of the year's rain. The record low is 4 degrees and the record high is 110. Heating, windows and roof drainage are sensible things to have answers about before a buyer asks.

What do Census numbers say about Sierra Vista homes?

Home values here sit well below the Phoenix-area cities, and rent is higher than in border towns such as San Luis. The Census Bureau reports these figures for 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

A 62 percent ownership rate means nearly four in ten households rent, so rentals are a real share of the market. Public schools come from the Sierra Vista Unified School District, which runs Buena High School, one middle school and six elementary schools. Higher education is available at Cochise College and the University of Arizona College of Applied Science and Technology.

What Sierra Vista city rules apply to a sale or a rental?

Repairs go through Community Development, which you can reach at (520) 417-4413 if you are unsure whether a project needs a permit. The city asks for plans as one complete, editable PDF with no passwords. Work in the public right-of-way and pool or spa drain applications go to the Public Works Department, and home-based business permits run through the City Clerk.

Landlords should know how the city treats rental income. The city's published property tax rate is $0.1056 per $100 of assessed value and its sales tax rate is 1.95 percent. A property owner who uses a management company can operate under that company's city business license. An owner who manages the property and must collect and remit real property rental tax needs a city business license of their own. The city is a program city, so the Arizona Department of Revenue collects the privilege taxes, and the city cannot give binding tax opinions.

Arizona law also limits what a city can require of short-term rentals (A.R.S. 9-500.39), including a permit fee capped at $250 or the actual cost and proof of $500,000 in liability coverage. Ask the City Clerk whether your buyer needs a permit for nightly rentals.

How do you record a Sierra Vista sale in Cochise County?

The deed is recorded with the Cochise County Recorder. A.R.S. 11-1133 requires a completed affidavit of property value with each deed, and the recorder must refuse a deed that lacks one unless it notes an exemption under A.R.S. 11-1134. Exemptions include:

  • A deed of gift
  • A conveyance made under a court order
  • A transfer for only nominal consideration between parent and child, spouses, or siblings

The standard recording fee under A.R.S. 11-475 is $30 per instrument. Ask the Recorder for the current mail-in and electronic filing steps, and let your title company confirm the total on the closing statement.

After the deed is recorded, the Cochise County Assessor changes the owner's name on the tax roll. If the old owner receives a tax notice after the sale, the Treasurer asks that it be returned to P.O. Box 1778, Bisbee, AZ 85603 with a note that the property sold.

When are Cochise County property taxes due for a Sierra Vista home?

Cochise County bills in two installments, and a combined bill covers the city, county, schools, college and special districts. Tax notices are mailed in September, and the county asks you to call if yours has not arrived by October 10. Taxes are due whether or not a notice arrives.

Source: Cochise County Treasurer FAQ and A.R.S. 42-18052. A weekend or holiday date moves to the next business day, so November 1, 2026 became Monday, November 2, and the first-half date has now passed.

After a delinquency date, simple interest runs at 16 percent a year, charged as 1.333 percent a month. Taxes still unpaid after May 1 and into the following January take a further 5 percent penalty, and the county sells its lien on delinquent parcels each February. The Treasurer notes that the tax lien attaches to the property each January no matter who owns it, so ask for a current balance before you sign a contract. If you think your value is wrong, an appeal concerns the property's value, and it starts when the notice of value arrives. Contact the Cochise County Assessor for that process.

It affects who is looking. The post is the city's main employer and nearly half of local jobs are in government. Set your price and closing date with that in mind, and ask each buyer for a written closing date.

Do I need a city business license to rent my Sierra Vista house?

It depends on how you manage it. If a property management company handles the rental, you can operate under its city business license. If you manage it yourself and must collect and remit real property rental tax, you need your own city license. Call Community Development or the City Clerk to confirm.

What does it cost to record a deed in Cochise County?

Arizona sets the fee at $30 per instrument under A.R.S. 11-475, with copies at $1 per page and $3 for a certificate. Ask the Cochise County Recorder or your title company for current steps and any extra charges.

What happens if my Cochise County taxes are delinquent when I sell?

The delinquent amount carries interest at 16 percent a year and may be sold as a lien in February. Because the lien attaches to the property each January, ask the Cochise County Treasurer for a payoff figure and have your title company handle payment at closing.

Yes. Arizona does not require repairs before a sale, so you can sell as-is. A financed buyer may ask for repairs after an inspection, while a cash buyer builds them into the offer. Work done without a permit is worth raising with Community Development at (520) 417-4413 before you list.

The city's 2014 financial report listed the Gadsden Elementary School District, ACT Advanced Call Center Technologies and the Arizona State Prison Complex in Yuma as its largest employers, each with roughly 800 or more staff. Highway access is through U.S. 95 and State Route 195 to Yuma, and Yuma County Area Transit connects to Greyhound in Yuma.

What do San Luis housing numbers look like?

Housing costs are modest and households are large. The Census Bureau figures below are for 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

MeasureSan Luis
Population, July 1, 2025 estimate42,030
Households9,562
Persons per household3.41
Owner-occupied housing rate68.4%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$224,900
Median gross rent$741
Median household income$59,400
Mean commute to work26.9 minutes

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, San Luis city, Arizona.

Two details matter for a seller. First, about 91 percent of residents speak a language other than English at home, so a listing, a disclosure packet or a contract explained in Spanish reaches more buyers. Second, the gap between a median home value of $224,900 and median rent of $741 is worth knowing when you set a price.

Which schools and neighborhoods will buyers ask about?

Most San Luis addresses feed the Gadsden Elementary School District, which runs Arizona Desert, Cesar Chavez, Desert View, Ed Pastor, Gadsden and Rio Colorado elementary schools plus San Luis Middle School and Southwest Junior High School. Sun Valley Elementary belongs to the Somerton Elementary School District, and San Luis High School is part of the Yuma Union High School District.

Buyers also look at:

  • Distance to the San Luis I port of entry for anyone who crosses regularly
  • The drive to Yuma on U.S. 95 or State Route 195
  • Whether the lot is in the newer eastern annexation area
  • Garage, shade and cooling equipment, given the heat

Ask your agent or buyer which school boundary applies to your street, since boundaries come from the school districts.

What city rules affect selling or fixing up a house in San Luis?

Repairs and additions go through the Building Safety Division, and land-use questions go to Planning and Zoning. Building Safety takes the permit application, a full set of plans or drawings that show the scope of work, and a site plan. Electronic PDF files are preferred, and hard copies run to two sets for residential work. The division can be reached at 928-341-8565. Planning and Zoning, at 1090 E. Union Street, handles land use applications, variances and temporary use permits and can be reached at 928-341-8563.

If you did work on the house without a permit, ask Building Safety what it needs before you list. A buyer's lender or inspector may raise it later.

Short-term renting is governed by state law. A.R.S. 9-500.39 bars a city from prohibiting short-term rentals but lets it require a permit with a fee of no more than $250 or the actual cost of issuing it, proof of $500,000 in liability coverage and an emergency contact. Ask the City of San Luis whether it runs such a permit if your buyer plans nightly rentals.

How is a San Luis sale transferred and recorded?

The deed is recorded with the Yuma County Recorder, and the recorder must refuse a deed that lacks a completed affidavit of property value unless it carries an exemption note (A.R.S. 11-1133). The affidavit is signed by seller and buyer or their agents and lists the sale price, financing type, parcel number and whether the home will be owner-occupied or rented.

Some transfers need no affidavit. Under A.R.S. 11-1134 the list includes:

  • A deed of gift
  • A transfer for only nominal consideration between parent and child, spouses, grandparent and grandchild, or siblings
  • A conveyance made under a court order
  • A deed that confirms or corrects one already recorded

The exemption has to be written on the face of the deed. The standard recording fee set by A.R.S. 11-475 is $30 per instrument, with copies at $1 a page and $3 for a certificate. Ask the Yuma County Recorder for current e-recording and mail-in instructions, and ask your title company to confirm the figure before closing.

When are property taxes due on a San Luis home?

Yuma County bills property tax in two halves. The first half is due October 1 and the second half March 1, and state law makes each half delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and May 1 (A.R.S. 42-18052). If a delinquency date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day, which is why the county calendar shows November 2, 2026 for the first half of 2026.

That date has now passed. Yuma County lists December 31 as the last day to pay 2026 taxes in full without interest, and the second half of 2026 is due March 1, 2027 and delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on May 3, 2027. Delinquent 2025 taxes pick up a 5 percent penalty on January 1, 2027 and go to the county tax lien sale on February 18, 2027.

Ask the Yuma County Treasurer for the current balance on your parcel before you sign a contract, and ask the title company how the current year will be split between you and the buyer.

More questions about San Luis, AZ

Do I need to make repairs before selling a house in San Luis?

No law requires repairs before a sale, so you can sell as-is. What changes is who buys. A buyer using a lender will usually ask for repairs after an inspection, while a cash buyer prices the repairs into the offer. If you did any past work without a permit, call the San Luis Building Safety Division at 928-341-8565 first.

Who records the deed when a San Luis house sells?

The Yuma County Recorder does. The deed must come with a completed affidavit of property value or a written exemption, and the standard fee under A.R.S. 11-475 is $30 per instrument. A title or escrow company normally handles the filing.

Is there a transfer tax when selling in San Luis?

Arizona law requires an affidavit of property value and a recording fee when a deed is recorded. Ask your title company for the full closing statement so you can see every charge before you sign.

What happens if I fall behind on Yuma County property taxes?

Taxes unpaid after the delinquency date are penalized and, in time, sold as a lien. For 2025 taxes, Yuma County lists a 5 percent penalty on January 1, 2027 and a tax lien sale on February 18, 2027. Contact the Yuma County Treasurer for a payoff figure.

Can the buyer of my San Luis house use it as a short-term rental?

Often yes, because A.R.S. 9-500.39 stops Arizona cities from banning short-term rentals. A city may still require a permit, insurance of at least $500,000 and an emergency contact. The buyer should ask the City of San Luis what applies.

How do you sell a house fast in Kingman, AZ?

Most Kingman sellers who want speed choose between listing with an agent and selling directly to a cash buyer, and the paperwork is the same either way. Kingman is the seat of Mohave County, so the deed recorder, the assessor, the treasurer and the courts all sit within a few blocks of each other downtown.

The city had an estimated 35,829 residents on July 1, 2025, up 9.6 percent from the April 2020 base, according to the Census Bureau. Owners occupy 68.4 percent of homes, and the median value of an owner-occupied home for 2020 to 2024 was $267,700. A five-year survey figure lags the street, so treat it as a rough anchor and ask a local agent or appraiser what comparable Kingman sales look like now.

A listing gives the widest buyer pool but depends on showings, a buyer's loan and an appraisal. A cash sale usually skips the loan and the appraisal, which shortens the calendar, though the offer reflects the buyer taking on repairs and risk. Whichever route you pick, gather these before you start:

  • Your recorded deed and the Mohave County parcel number
  • Payoff figures for any mortgage, home equity line or lien
  • Permit records for work done on the house
  • HOA or special district contacts, if the lot has any
  • The most recent property tax bill

What is Kingman like for a home seller?

Kingman is a high-desert railroad and highway town of about 37.5 square miles at roughly 3,471 feet, set in the Hualapai Valley between the Cerbat and Hualapai mountain ranges. It was founded in 1882 as a railroad siding and takes its name from Lewis Kingman, a civil engineer who supervised track building for the Atlantic and Pacific Railroad, per Wikipedia.

Buyers find Kingman through its roads. Interstate 40 and U.S. 93 meet here, with Flagstaff 147 miles east, Needles, California 62 miles southwest and Las Vegas 107 miles northwest. Postwar growth came from a former Army airfield turned industrial park and a vehicle proving ground in nearby Yucca opened in 1955, and several neighborhoods were built to house the workers.

The climate matters when you prepare a house. Kingman sits at the eastern edge of the Mojave Desert but at a plateau elevation, so summer highs rarely pass 107 degrees while winter nights often drop below freezing and snow is possible. Average yearly precipitation is about 8 inches. A storm on December 31, 2014 and January 1, 2015 left 6.5 inches of snow and closed Interstate 40 at the U.S. 93 junction for 24 hours. A buyer's inspector will look at the heating system, pipe insulation and roof as closely as the air conditioner.

What do Kingman housing numbers look like?

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures give a plain picture of who lives in Kingman homes and what they pay. They help you judge whether your price and terms fit the local buyer base.

About 84 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most buyers and sellers already know the town. The median gross rent of $1,058 is a useful check if you expect an investor to weigh your house as a rental.

Which permits and city rules affect selling a Kingman house?

Work done without a permit is the item most likely to slow a Kingman sale. The city's Development Services Department runs the Building Division, which accepts applications for residential, commercial, industrial, demolition and signage work. Call (928) 753-8130 to ask about an address before you list. The division also publishes a residential permit process guide that explains the Minor Improvement Permit, which covers smaller jobs.

Inspections are scheduled by phone, and the city asks for the request before 7:00 a.m. on the day you want the inspector, with your permit number and job site address ready. If a patio cover, room addition or garage conversion was built years ago, ask the city what it has on file and what a retroactive permit would require. Fixing that before an offer arrives avoids a renegotiation at inspection.

Short-term rentals inside city limits need a city permit under Ordinance No. 1952, effective October 1, 2023. The city's rental page lists a $60 annual fee, a Transaction Privilege Tax license, a 24-hour emergency contact and written notice to neighboring homes. Operating without a permit can bring fines of up to $1,000 a month. A buyer who plans to rent by the night will ask whether your property has a permit, so be ready to say yes or no.

If the house sits outside the city in unincorporated Mohave County, a different rule can apply. State law requires a seller of five or fewer parcels of land, other than subdivided land, in an unincorporated area to give the buyer a written affidavit of disclosure at least seven days before transfer, with a five-day rescission right for the buyer, under A.R.S. 33-422.

How are deeds recorded and taxes handled in Mohave County?

Deeds are recorded at the Mohave County Recorder, 700 West Beale Street in Kingman, and the office lists a $30 fee for recording documents. Arizona law requires an Affidavit of Property Value to be attached to a deed that transfers title, unless the deed carries an exemption notation, under A.R.S. 11-1133. The recorder refuses a deed without one. Your title or escrow company normally prepares both, and the recorder's FAQ notes that staff cannot give legal advice on how to fill out forms.

The same page says the recorder's self-service search will show recorded liens by name, but a search does not prove the property is clear, so buyers rely on title insurance. Copies of a recorded deed cost $1.00 per page.

Property tax is billed by the Mohave County Treasurer. The Treasurer's FAQ sets these dates:

  • First half due October 1 and past due after 5:00 p.m. on November 1, moving to the next business day when that falls on a weekend. November 1, 2026 was a Sunday, so that deadline has already passed this year.
  • Second half due March 1 and past due after 5:00 p.m. on May 1.
  • Bills over $100 paid in one payment by December 31 owe no interest accrued after November 1.
  • Late payments carry 16 percent annual interest, prorated monthly.

Ask the escrow officer how the current year's tax will be prorated at closing. If you receive a bill after the sale, the Treasurer asks that you forward it to the new owner or return it to P.O. Box 712, Kingman, AZ 86402 with a note about the sale. The Assessor at 928-753-0703 can confirm the sale was recorded.

Who buys Kingman houses that need work?

Investors and cash buyers are the usual buyers for Kingman houses with deferred repairs, tenants in place, an inherited title or a looming payment problem. They price the work and the time into their offer, so expect a number below a fully repaired retail sale in exchange for speed and fewer conditions.

Compare offers on net proceeds. Ask each buyer who pays escrow and title charges, how long the buyer needs to close, whether the buyer will accept the house as is and what happens to the deposit if the buyer backs out. Get the offer in writing and read the contract before you sign. If you are behind on a mortgage, ask your lender for a payoff figure and the sale deadline first, since the calendar sets your options.

Kingman Unified School District No. 20 runs 13 schools and reports 6,734 students on its district site, and families with children will ask about the assigned school. Mohave Community College also has one of its campuses in the city.

More questions about Kingman, AZ

Can I sell my Kingman house without making repairs?

Yes, you can offer the house as is. A buyer using a loan may ask for repairs after an appraisal or inspection, while investors and cash buyers often accept a house in its current condition. Open permits and unpermitted additions can still delay closing, so call Kingman Development Services at (928) 753-8130 to check your address.

How long does recording a deed take in Mohave County?

The recorder checks each document against the recording requirements in A.R.S. 11-480 and, if it is complete and the fee is paid, assigns a recording number. Mailed originals come back in about 4 to 6 weeks, while in-person documents are returned after scanning. Your escrow company usually handles recording on closing day.

Do I owe property tax if I sell in the middle of the year?

Ask your escrow officer how the year's tax will be split between you and the buyer. Mohave County bills are due October 1 and March 1, with the first half past due after November 1. The settlement statement should show the split.

Does Kingman allow short-term rentals?

Yes, with a permit. The city requires a permit, a Transaction Privilege Tax license, an emergency contact and neighbor notice for rentals under 30 days inside city limits. Arizona law at A.R.S. 9-500.39 limits how far a city may restrict them, but a permit is allowed. The city's rental page lists a $60 annual fee.

Who do I call about a lien or a title question on a Kingman property?

Start with a title company, because the recorder's staff cannot give legal advice or do research for you. The Mohave County Recorder at (928) 753-0701 can show you how to run a basic search by name, and a title company can tell you whether liens or judgments will cut into your proceeds.
